title: A Pragmatic Phase II Study to Optimize Neoadjuvant Treatment and Surgical De-escalation in HR+/HER2− Early Breast Cancer Using Oncotype DX and Abemaciclib
official: A Pragmatic Phase II Study to Optimize Neoadjuvant Treatment and Surgical De-escalation in HR+/HER2− Early Breast Cancer Using Oncotype DX and Abemaciclib - VIOLET trial
summary:
Main objective: -to determine the proportion of patients with ER+ (≥10%)/HER2− EBC who can avoid neoadjuvant and adjuvant chemotherapy through MDT-guided use of NET plus abemaciclib based on the ODX RS obtained from the initial diagnostic biopsy 
- to evaluate the proportion of patients achieving surgical de-escalation after neoadjuvant therapy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Female, aged 18 years or older,
2. Adequate hematologic, renal, and hepatic function as defined below. Normal hematologic parameters: a. absolute neutrophil count ≥1500/mm3 (1.5 × 10 9/L), b. platelets ≥ 100 × 10 9/L, Ver. 1.0, 25.02.2026 21 c. hemoglobin ≥ 8 g/dL (≥ 80 g/L)). Patients may receive erythrocyte transfusions to achieve this hemoglobin level at the discretion of the investigator. Initial treatment must not begin earlier than the day after the erythrocyte transfusion
3. Normal renal function: serum creatinine concentration ≤1.5 ULN or calculated creatinine clearance ≥50 mL/min according to the Cockcroft-Gault formula,
4. Normal liver function: a. serum total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN). Patients with Gilbert’s syndrome with a total bilirubin ≤2.0 times ULN and direct bilirubin within normal limits are permitted, b. AST and ALT ≤ 3 × ULN, c. alkaline phosphatase ≤ 2.5 × ULN,
5. Women of childbearing potential must have documented negative pregnancy test within 2 weeks (preferably 7 days) prior to study entry and must agree to effective non-hormonal contraception (barrier method – condoms, diaphragm –also in conjunction with spermicidal jelly, or total abstinence) after the pregnancy test and up to surgery. Oral, injectable, or implant hormonal contraceptives or medicated IUD are not allowed during the trial,
6. Menopausal status must be documented according to standard clinical criteria (age, menstrual history, or laboratory confirmation when clinically indicated)
7. Willingness to undergo breast surgery after optimal neoadjuvant treatment
8. Willingness to provide blood and tumor samples for the study purposes, including submission for central Oncotype Dx assessment
9. primary, histologically confirmed diagnosis of invasive breast carcinoma
10. Estrogen receptor (ER)-positive tumor, defined as ≥10% by immunohistochemistry according to ASCO/CAP guidelines (Allison et al.2020). Any progesterone receptor expression is acceptable (per local assessment)
11. HER2-negative tumor, documented and assessed locally according to ASCO/CAP guidelines
12. Stage II-IIIB disease according to AJCC TNM classification (8th edition). Absence of distant metastases (with the exception of tumor detected in internal mammary chain nodes by sentinel node procedure),
13. Candidate to receive neoadjuvant chemotherapy according to the indication of a multidisciplinary tumor board
14. Not eligible to receive upfront BCS but potentially eligible to receive a BCS in case of tumor downstaging AND/OR not candidate to SLND due to clinical node positive disease
15. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status 0-1
16. Ability to swallow oral medications
Exclusion criteria:
1. Presence of distant metastases (stage IV) or stage IIIC disease,
2. Active systemic infection, including bacterial infection requiring intravenous [IV] antibiotics at the time of initiating study treatment, fungal infection, or detectable viral infection (such as known human immunodeficiency virus positivity or with known active hepatitis B or C (for example, hepatitis B surface antigen positive)
3. Contraindications or known hypersensitivity to the trial medication or excipients
4. Inflammatory or locally-advanced, inoperable breast cancer
5. Previous invasive ipsilateral breast cancer at any time,
6. Previous or concomitant invasive malignancy, except for patients with the following (and only the following) malignancies (previous or concomitant), if adequately treated: a. basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, b. melanoma in situ, c. in situ non-breast carcinoma without invasion, d. contra- or ipsilateral in situ breast carcinoma, e. non-breast invasive malignancy diagnosed at least 5 years ago and without recurrence, f. stage I papillary thyroid cancer, g. stage Ia carcinoma of the cervix, h. stage Ia or b endometrioid endometrial cancer, i. borderline or stage I ovarian cancer,
7. Known history of clinically significant cardiovascular disease, including but not limited to: uncontrolled or symptomatic angina, uncontrolled hypertension (≥ 180/110 mmHg), uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, dyspnea at rest, chronic oxygen therapy, a New York Heart Association (NYHA) class III or IV congestive heart failure, syncope of cardiovascular etiology, ventricular arrhythmia of pathological origin (including ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation), or sudden cardiac arrest.
8. Women who are pregnant or lactating. If applicable, lactation must be discontinued before study entry
9. Presence of serious and/or uncontrolled preexisting medical condition(s) that, in the judgment of the investigator, would preclude participation in this study (for example, interstitial lung disease, severe dyspnea at rest or requiring oxygen therapy, severe renal impairment [e.g. estimated creatinine clearance <30ml/min], history of major surgical resection involving the stomach or small bowel, or preexisting Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis or a preexisting chronic condition resulting in baseline Grade 2 or higher diarrhea)
10. Major surgery within 14 days prior to study entry
11. The patient has received an experimental treatment in a clinical trial within the last 30 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, prior to study entry, or is currently enrolled in any other type of medical research (for example: medical device) judged by the sponsor not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study
